Senses.PreferredTarget: the numinous turtle drags its tail
AlternateTargets: the spirit turtle leaves a trail with its tail
the marvelous turtle betrays itself by dragging its tail
Senses.Note: Six direct deployments span six independent works.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直饒眼似流星。機如掣電。未免靈龜曳尾。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2003.xml). Blue Cliff Record by Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo. Yuanwu Keqin says that even meteor-like eyes and lightning function do not escape the turtle’s dragged tail.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若言有道有心，猶是把箸拈匙見識；若言無心無道，依然靈龜曳尾之機。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB406.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianran of Mount Lu. Tianran says that asserting no mind and no Way still shows the mechanism of the turtle dragging its tail.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: Tianran of Mount Lu: The book title and enclosing 上堂 identify Tianran as the speaker of the exact clause; no canonical roster key is asserted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 印空印泥印水，平地寒濤競起。假饒去就十分，也是靈龜曳尾。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X84/X84n1583.xml). Orthodox Continuation of the Lamp. Jianmen Nan answers a question on the three seals by saying that even perfect handling is the turtle dragging its tail.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: Jianmen Nan: The complete biographical unit names 劍門南修道者 and 南曰 assigns him the exact answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云藏身處兮沒蹤踪沒踪跡處不藏身如何是入身句師云靈龜曳尾自取喪身之兆
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (L/L158/L158n1652.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mingjue Cong. Mingjue Cong answers the requested entry-into-body phrase by calling the dragged tail a self-made omen of losing the body.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只如雪竇恁麼道，已是靈龜曳尾。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1301.xml). Record of Fogu’s Beat-the-Rhythm Sections. Yuanwu Keqin says that Xuedou’s added judgment is already the numinous turtle dragging its tail.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大小演祖大似靈龜曳尾，一言既落人耳，如何諱得？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1308.xml). Path-Stone: Dripping Milk Collection. Dawei Jinglun says Wuzu Fayan resembles the numinous turtle dragging its tail because words already heard cannot be disowned.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The enclosing section names 五臺山顯通大巍淨倫禪師, and the first-person 示眾 assigns Dawei Jinglun the exact verdict.

Senses.Explanation: The numinous turtle drags its tail and thereby leaves the trace that betrays it. Chan masters use the image when an apparently quick, subtle, or traceless performance still exposes a residual mark by which it can be caught. Yuanwu says even lightning-fast eyes and function do not escape it; Tianran applies it to assertions of either mind and Way or no mind and no Way; Jianmen Nan says even perfect handling of the three seals leaves the tail; and Mingjue Cong calls an entry-answer the turtle’s self-made omen of ruin. Yuanwu also applies it to Xuedou’s added comment, and Dawei Jinglun uses it for Wuzu Fayan’s saying that cannot be retracted once heard.
